fields.text: Initial meeting with Sarah Chen. She showed photos of a similar desk they saw at a hotel in Tokyo. Wants warm wood tones with subtle lighting. Budget discussed around $12-15k.
Estimate generated. Material costs came in higher than expected due to white oak prices. May need to discuss with Sarah if total exceeds budget.
Sarah confirmed acceptance by email. She chose the satin finish over the gloss option. Start date agreed: next Monday.
Sarah prefers email over phone. Best reached before 10am.
Meridian has done 3 projects with us previously. Good payment history. Marcus handles AP.
White oak shipment arrived, checking for defects before milling.
Derek wants something old-fashioned looking. Showed reference photos of signs in North Beach.
Client did not pay deposit within 30 days. Attempted follow-up calls on 3/1 and 3/7 with no response.
Tomoko picked up the pieces. She was happy with the cuts, may have more work coming.
Ray dropped off rough sketches. Wants to be able to swap out panels when they change the tap list. Needs to survive a humid taproom.
Good local client. Tomoko handles project decisions, Ray handles facilities and logistics.
Event rental company. Priya manages client projects, Ben runs the warehouse. They rent furniture and decor for weddings and corporate events.
Ben wants these ASAP but budget is tight. Discussed using construction-grade lumber to keep costs down. Needs to hold 500lbs per shelf.
Priya needs these before wedding season starts in June. Wants them to look upscale but be durable enough for weekly rentals. Showed photos of bars at a recent gala.
Priya ordered 10 to start. If clients like them she will order 20 more. Needs a sample by end of month.
Design complete. All parts cut. Currently shaping and sanding — about halfway through the batch.
Hotel management group. Elena handles all FF&E procurement for renovations. Net 30 terms, always pays on time. Big potential for repeat work.
Elena sent architectural drawings from their designer. Panels need to match existing millwork in the elevator lobby. White oak sourced from same mill as original build.
Elena wants these to match the lobby panels project. Same white oak, same finish. Upholstery subcontracted to her preferred vendor after we build the frames.
Deposit invoice sent to Elena. She said AP will process within 2 weeks. Not starting fabrication until deposit clears.
James found us through Yelp. Wants a pergola but seems surprised by custom pricing. Mentioned a Home Depot kit as an alternative.
James called back — says the estimate is way above his budget. Going to buy a kit from a big box store instead. Politely declined to negotiate.
Owns Spice Route restaurant on Alberta. Hands-on owner, very particular about design. Prefers texting over email.
Aisha closing the restaurant for 2 weeks for renovation. Counter needs to be ready for install on day 3 of the closure. Very tight timeline.
All fabrication complete. Counter installed during closure week, Aisha is thrilled. Need to generate final invoice for remaining balance.
Follow-up project from the counter job. Aisha wants the same walnut and steel look for a spice display behind the register. Small job, quick turnaround.
Installed and looks great. Aisha posted photos on Instagram. Final invoice sent, awaiting payment.

fields.name: 03006 - Omnicom Aluminum perf wall
fields.description:
Finally price has been agreed on, $1750 per panel for a total of $8750 for all 5.  No money for processing the drawings so if they send a file that we need to trim we will send it back to be fixed.  Neal to come in and help cut, and we will split the price with him.  He may have negotiated terms of On Receipt for this job as Martinelli has a bad record of payment, and because this is still like half of what we should be charging.
(Neal's CNC - 09/02/2015)

fields.name: 03006 - Perf Wall Prototype
fields.description:
Tim Tait sending a second aluminum square to arrive on Tuesday.  We are to cut the same file as before but with a 1/4" bit instead of a 1/8.  PO is for $500 again, which is fine as the bigger bit can go faster.

IF WE HAVE A CHANCE, estimate the whole thing with a 1/4" bit to see how much we *should* charge for it.  Previously Neal agreed to $8k for the full set of 5 panels, but we later worked out that was way too little and told them it had to be more.  Partially bc they originally said it was 1/8" aluminum but later changed that to 3/16".
(Neal's CNC - 07/17/2015)
First prototype was Neal's job.  If we get the complete wall project, which seems more likely now that they've asked for a second prototype, Neal will come help and we will split it.  The second prototype is maybe all ours?
(Neal's CNC - 07/18/2015)
1/4" bit version was cut with 2 passes for file1, at .89 and .07.  Speed set at 70 but bumped to 105.  File2 was 1 pass to depth of 1.01.  There were two small imperfections in the result which I traced to the cut file, and put a note there.  It only happened for very short lines, but not for all the very short lines.  Something to do with the ramp-in for the second pass.
(Neal's CNC - 08/13/2015)

fields.name: Cave
fields.description:
After having broken up about 1/4 of the parts and added joins, which took 5 hours, I calculated that the cost with half laps is about 2.8 times the cost without.  Which would put their estimate at $4k x 2.8 = $11.2k.  Devin suggested cutting only the edge of the half lap and having his contractor cut out the bulk of the material (unclear exactly how, but not our problem).  I suggested a dogleg butt join instead of the half lap.  I will sketch both of those, send him the pic, and he will discuss with his contractor.
(Neal's CNC - 10/27/2017)
Dogleg joins were decided on

This Job was particularly difficult for a number of reasons.  
Notification was made on Friday Oct 6 that parts were needed for a soft deadline of Tuesday, and a hard deadline of Wed Oct 11.  

Materials specd was 4140 steel.  McMaster delivered (on monday) 4142 HARDENED which has a hardness of 230.  Machining feedrates had to be slowed 50 percent opposite of a 4140 steel.  

Machining started Monday afternoon and continued into the late night.  

Two pairs were delivered on Wed morning, and the third pair was delivered Wed afternoon

Work started on the remaining 4 pairs Wednesday afternoon, and overtime was also accrued.   The remaining 4 pairs were to be machined from whole block of 4142 and turned on the lathe after roughing and finishing.  The remaining 4 pairs were delivered Friday Morning.  It is my belief that the units made the shipping deadline.

Construct base and topper for display case, approximately 11-1/2' long, 3' deep, and 8' tall, with one angled bend, approximately 22.5°, in the middle.

Proposed build process:
* draw/update 3d model; "detail" 3d model into specific parts to be CNC cut
* cut parts from 3/4" plywood or other appropriate thickness ply
* assemble base, with groove around upper edge to accept 3/8" acrylic mid-section (from other vendor)
* assemble topper, with a groove around the bottom edge to sit atop the 3/8" acrylic mid-section, a removable bottom from which the artwork can be hung, and a removable top panel to protect from dust or objects being thrown into the case
* sand and fill any gaps or uneven areas on all visible surfaces
* roll on 1 coat primer and 2 coats SFMOMA shade of white paint on all visible surfaces (resulting in "orange peel" surface, similar to a normal building interior wall)
* place acrylic mid-sections in finished position and verify groove is correct in base and topper; alter grooves if needed; paint interior of grooves
* palletize all parts and package for delivery

Construct base and topper for display case, approximately 11' long, 3'4" deep, and 8' tall.

Proposed build process:
* draw/update 3d model; "detail" 3d model into specific parts to be CNC cut
* cut parts from 3/4" plywood or other appropriate thickness ply
* assemble base, with groove around upper edge to accept 3/8" acrylic mid-section (from other vendor)
* assemble topper, with a groove around the bottom edge to sit atop the 3/8" acrylic mid-section, a removable bottom from which the artwork can be hung, and a removable top panel to protect from dust or objects being thrown into the case
* sand and fill any gaps or uneven areas on all visible surfaces
* roll on 1 coat primer and 2 coats SFMOMA shade of white paint on all visible surfaces (resulting in "orange peel" surface, similar to a normal building interior wall)
* place acrylic mid-sections in finished position and verify groove is correct in base and topper; alter grooves if needed; paint interior of grooves
* palletize all parts and package for delivery
**Neal's CNC understands that the clear acrylic mid-section for the two cases will be constructed and delivered to Neal's CNC's shop by other SFMOMA vendors**

This Job was particularly difficult for a number of reasons.  
Notification was made on Friday Oct 6 that parts were needed for a soft deadline of Tuesday, and a hard deadline of Wed Oct 11.  

Materials specd was 4140 steel.  McMaster delivered (on monday) 4142 HARDENED which has a hardness of 230.  Machining feedrates had to be slowed 50 percent opposite of a 4140 steel.  

Machining started Monday afternoon and continued into the late night.  

Two pairs were delivered on Wed morning, and the third pair was delivered Wed afternoon

Work started on the remaining 4 pairs Wednesday afternoon, and overtime was also accrued.   The remaining 4 pairs were to be machined from whole block of 4142 and turned on the lathe after roughing and finishing.  The remaining 4 pairs were delivered Friday Morning.  It is my belief that the units made the shipping deadline.
